findings.title: Continuing provision as an exploratory analogy
findings.claim: In an attributed, exploratory analogy, repeated sign-dispatch resembles a continuing yield associated with the she-camel, while denial imagines that flow failing.
findings.mechanism: The form-distant milk branches meet the two focus sending occurrences, the denial verb, and the literal camel placed between them; the expected-flow facet turns falsification into interrupted provision.
findings.reader_payoff: Before, the signs are abstract proofs and the camel a disconnected example; after, the ayah can also be pictured as dispatch of continuing provision that is not received as expected.
findings.containment: This is only an HFT-nominated material analogy. It does not make milk the lexical meaning of the sending or denial verbs, nor claim a historical camel-milk event; every HFT coordinate and role remains legacy_unbound.

epistemic.reason: The packet marks this as a surprising outlier with form-distant branches and missing target morphology; retain only as attributed analogy.

branch_activations.boundary: This is an attributed analogy, not the lexical denotation of nursilu or nursila.
